Tag a data frame as carrying edit-history provenance

Source: R/classes.R
new_edited_data.Rd

Prepends the edited_data class to a frame that has an edits attribute, so printing it shows a provenance banner. Every editor tags its output automatically.

Usage

new_edited_data(df)

# S3 method for class 'edited_data'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

df

A data frame, typically fresh from an editor.

x

An edited_data object.

...

Passed to the next print method.

Value

df with the edited_data class prepended when an edits attribute is present; df unchanged otherwise.

What keeps the history

These rules are verified by test (test-port-tier2.R) rather than asserted, because most of them depend on S3 dispatch finding a lifr method, and that depends on which argument carries the class.

Kept:

  • [ – rows, columns, or both.

  • The dplyr verbs – filter(), mutate(), select(), arrange(), and the joins – through dplyr_reconstruct().

  • rbind(), when its first argument is an edited_data or lif_data frame: then every argument's history is concatenated in argument order. This is the one operation that merges two histories.

Lost:

  • rbind() when the first argument is a plain data frame or tibble. rbind.data.frame is dispatched instead, and the result silently carries no class and no history at all – not even the classed argument's. Put the edited frame first.

  • dplyr::bind_rows() keeps at most the first argument's history and never concatenates two. Use rbind() to combine edited frames.

  • merge(), and rebuilding a frame from its columns.

  • tibble::as_tibble() and as.data.frame() drop the class, so the provenance banner stops printing. The attribute itself usually survives, and edit_history() will still read it, but nothing maintains it from then on: a declassed frame placed first in rbind() keeps only its own history and silently drops the rest.

Use lif_get_edits() / lif_set_edits() around the operations that lose it.

See also

edit_history()

Examples

d  <- data.frame(boring = "B1", depth = 1:3, signal = c(5, 0, 2))
ed <- lif_zero_shallow(d, depth = 1)
#> [lif_zero_shallow] changed 1 reading(s) at or above 1 ft across 1 boring(s)
inherits(ed, "edited_data")
#> [1] TRUE
nrow(edit_history(ed[, c("boring", "depth", "signal")]))
#> [1] 1
